usual_baseline: Core items (surgeon, date, procedure, findings) are near 100%. The same few items fail: blood loss 0–8% [2193, 2299, 2426, 2770], time of operation 0–9% [2193, 2295, 2500], elective/emergency 0–10% [1626, 2193, 2235], DVT prophylaxis 6% [2233]. Overall compliance about 50–72% [1586, 1276, 2295]; full compliance 4–7% [2250, 2820].
fix_that_works: A typed or electronic template with mandatory or drop-down fields. Overall 50% to 92% [1586]; below 80% to above 98% [2256]; 37.5% to 83.3% [2553]; 67% to 94% [2803]; full compliance 7% to 85% of template notes [2820]; 35% to 89% in template notes [2490]. Easy online access plus induction: 69% to 96.6% [2738].
fix_that_fails: Teaching or presentation alone: all items stayed well below standard, time 3% to 6.67% [2595]; knee 71% to 74%, hip 68% to 64% [1227]. Blood loss stayed at 8% despite a template [1136]. Templates are bypassed: use fell 45% to 28% [2146]; tonsillectomy proforma 33% [2095]. Gains fell at 24 months as new staff missed the template [1366].
consultant_advice: One of the most overdone audits, with 65 here and the same answer. Don't audit RCS items again. Audit whether a template is still used a year on and by new staff, or procedure-specific GIRFT items and whether notes reach the ward on time.
